summary: Every charm in the store costs 1 ticket less while this is equipped.
tip: Strong economy: about one free charm for every few you buy. With drawers, keep it stored and equip it only while shopping.

synergies.why: Cheap or free charms to buy and discard feed Dung Beetle.
Each Cigarettes buy costs 1 less; the first one each Deadline is free.
More purchases per ticket grow its Ticket chance faster.
Its permanent -1 store discount stacks with this one, so cheap charms can become free.
Surgery (DLC): Fidelity Card + Dear Diary fuse into VIP Card.

assumptions: Prices can drop to 0, so 1-ticket charms become free.

summary: Does nothing on the machine; it only sells for twice the normal ticket value.
tip: Skip it unless you run CloverField or Dark Lotus, or plan to fuse it with Property Certificate into Beach Hotel (DLC).

synergies.why: Its +1 resell value per Round counts double on Sardines.
The doubled resell value adds straight to Dark Lotus's Symbols Multiplier.
Surgery (DLC): Sardines + Property Certificate fuse into Beach Hotel (+3 charm space).
That memory card makes Sardines always come with a Trait.

assumptions: Base resell value depends on cost and Trait; the exact formula is unknown.

summary: 35% chance each spin that every Pattern triggers one extra time.
tip: A reliable boost for any build. Even better with Golden/Chain symbols, pattern-count charms, and Horseshoe (70%).

synergies.why: Doubles its trigger chance to 70%.
Red Button forces the retrigger on the next spin.
Retriggered spins reach 5+ Patterns more often, growing Pentacle.
Doubling the pattern count helps reach 7+ Patterns.
Retriggers score Chain symbols again, so pattern values grow twice.

summary: Patterns Multiplier +1 for each equipped charm that has a Trait.
tip: Great when Traits keep coming (trait phone calls, Expensive Love, Holy Spirit). Weak with only 0-1 traited charms.

synergies.why: Every store charm has a Trait, so each purchase adds Patterns Multiplier.
Each 999 puts a Trait on every charm on the table.
Traits the whole store; even the Devious it adds to you counts.
Ambitious gives +1 Patterns Multiplier, and +1 more through The Collector.
Adds a Devious Trait to a random table charm every Deadline: another Trait for The Collector to count, at the cost of more 666 risk.
Surgery (DLC): The Collector + Dark Lotus fuse into Graded Card (Avid/Ambitious bonuses become x2).

antiSynergies.why: Store charms cannot spawn with Traits in that run.
Store and drawer charms cannot spawn with Traits.

assumptions: Any Trait counts, including Devious.

summary: Every time charms activate 5 times in a Round, your next spin gets Luck +7.
tip: Only pays off on a busy board: random-trigger charms, cats, Red Button charms. Too slow with few active charms.

synergies.why: Random-trigger charms fire twice as often, reaching 5 activations sooner.
One press fires every random-trigger charm at once.
35% per-spin activation that also retriggers Patterns.
Fires on about 30% of spins, a cheap steady activation source.

assumptions: Read as 5 charm activations (not 5 different charms), counted per Round.
The Luck +7 applies to the spin after the 5th activation.

summary: After 3 spins without a 5+ symbol pattern, the next spin is forced to show an Above or Below pattern.
tip: Gives an 8-symbol pattern about every 4th spin, huge early. Pairs with Baphomet, Abstract Painting and large-pattern boosts.

synergies.why: Nose guarantees the Above/Below patterns that Baphomet doubles on each 666.
The forced 8-symbol pattern reliably triggers its pattern doubling.
The forced big pattern triggers Stain's +base to all Patterns for the Round.
Raises Above/Below (and other 4+ patterns) by base value.
Each forced 4+ symbol pattern permanently raises Diamonds and Treasures.
Each Diesel trigger adds +7 to Above and Below (their base value); Nose cashes one in every few spins.

assumptions: Approximated as a forced Above/Below every 4th spin. The real trigger is 3 straight spins without a 5+ symbol Pattern, so it fires less in builds that already land big patterns.
Assumes the forced pattern's symbol is picked by normal symbol chances.

summary: After scoring Diamonds, Treasures or Sevens 3 spins in a row, the next spin shows the Eye pattern.
tip: Only for builds that score gems nearly every spin: stack Diamond, Treasure or Seven chance first. Pareidolia or Eye of God turn the Eyes into big payoffs.

synergies.why: A lone Eye doubles all Patterns permanently; Eye Jar supplies the Eyes.
Each Eye pays out all coins earned from 999s again.
+1 Diamond chance makes the 3-spin gem streak much more common.
+1 Treasure chance helps keep the gem streak going.
Raises the Eye pattern's value by its base value.

antiSynergies.why: Halves Diamond, Treasure and Seven chances, breaking the streaks.
Blocks the most valuable symbol (usually Seven) from appearing.

assumptions: Any of Diamond, Treasure or Seven scored in each spin keeps the streak alive.

summary: Symbols Multiplier +1 for every phone reroll made this run. Rerolls cost tickets.
tip: A reroll costs Deadline-1 tickets, +1 per extra reroll that Deadline, and each adds +1 Symbols Multiplier for good: cheapest early, best with strong ticket income.

synergies.why: Doubles your tickets to fund many rerolls.
Ticket-modifier income pays for rerolls.

antiSynergies.why: Sets tickets to 0, leaving nothing for rerolls.
No ticket income from Rounds, so rerolls stay scarce.

assumptions: Counts phone rerolls from the whole run, including ones made before you bought it.

summary: Red Button (3 charges): each press gives Symbols Multiplier +1 permanently.
tip: Press it whenever it is full. Charge sources (Potato Battery, Electricity Meter) and Nuclear Button's double trigger turn it into steady scaling.

synergies.why: Each press triggers twice: +2 Symbols Multiplier.
Lowers its recharge from 3 charges to 2 (or 1 if taken twice).
Two missed spins in a row add a charge.
Store restocks can recharge it.
Half of the presses cost no charge.
Instantly refills it for another press.

assumptions: Charms regain 1 charge per Round, so without help it fires about once per Deadline.

summary: On spins with no Patterns, 25% chance to raise every symbol by its base value, permanently.
tip: Cheap early scaling that turns empty spins into value; it fires less once your build lands patterns every spin. Horseshoe doubles the odds.

synergies.why: Doubles its chance to 50% on empty spins.
Surgery (DLC): Consolation Prize + Midas Touch fuse into First Place Prize (40% per spin: scored symbols +base value).
Fewer lucky spins means more empty spins to trigger on.
An empty spin is also a miss toward Steam's 3-miss streak, so the same bad spins feed both symbol-value boosts.

assumptions: The 25% roll only happens on spins with zero Patterns.

summary: Symbols Multiplier +X, where X is the total resell value of all charms on the table.
tip: A big flat multiplier from the moment you equip it. With CloverField raising resell values every Round it keeps climbing.

synergies.why: +1 resell value per charm each Round, so the multiplier grows all run.
Double resell value means extra multiplier.
+2 charm space puts more resell value on the table.
+1 permanent slot for another charm's resell value.
Surgery (DLC): Dark Lotus + The Collector fuse into Graded Card.

assumptions: The exact resell formula is unknown. Ratings assume about 1-3 tickets per charm, so X is roughly 7-15 on a full table before CloverField.
Surgery charms have 0 resell value and add nothing.

summary: Red Button (12 charges): +1 Round this Deadline. Using it 5+ times in one Deadline discards it.
tip: Needs heavy recharging (Car Battery, Potato Battery, Electricity Meter). The 5th use in one Deadline still gives a Round but discards it, so stop at 4 to keep it.

effects.text: Triggering it 5 or more times in one Deadline discards it; it cannot reappear in the store until the next Deadline.

synergies.why: Each press triggers it twice: +2 Rounds, but both uses count toward the 5-per-Deadline limit.
Refills all 12 charges at once for another Round.
Discard it, then discard Vorago: it comes back fully charged with its per-Deadline use count reset.
Missed spins add charges toward the 12 it needs.
Store restocks feed its charges.
Surgery (DLC): Weird Clock + Corpse (Left Leg) fuse into Eternal Rest.

assumptions: Assumes it is bought fully charged, giving one Round right away; after that it needs 12 Rounds of natural recharge or other charge sources.

summary: Takes no space: instantly adds 1 extra Round to the current Deadline.
tip: Can save a Deadline you are about to fail. If you clear the debt early anyway, the extra Round is skipped for +4 tickets.

synergies.why: Abyssu banks a second activation: discard Abyssu later for another emergency Round.
If you clear the debt early, the extra Round counts as one more skip for Calendar.
An extra skippable Round raises its Golden chance.
Each extra Round you skip adds +4 to Golden Pepper's Luck roll next Deadline.

summary: Symbols Multiplier +2 per free restock you hold; gives 1 free restock at the start of every Deadline.
tip: Hoard free restocks instead of spending them. Crowbar, CloverBell and Ritual Bell feed it; browse with D6 or Cigarettes.

synergies.why: +3 free restocks = +6 Symbols Multiplier while you hold them.
Scoring Clovers and Bells together gives 3 free restocks at a time.
Each 666 gives 3 free restocks.
That memory card gives 2 free restocks every Deadline.
Refreshes the store every Round without spending your hoard.
Surgery (DLC): Shopping Cart + Fake Coin fuse into RWD Cart, a one-time doubling of the free restocks you hold (10% risk of losing them).

antiSynergies.why: Wants you to spend restocks, which shrinks the Cart's bonus.
Pays off for restocking, while the Cart pays for hoarding.

assumptions: The bonus counts free restocks you currently hold, so spending them lowers it.

summary: Takes no space: instantly gives 3 free store restocks.
tip: Cheap way to dig for key charms. Even better held unspent with Shopping Cart, or spent with Bell Pepper or Electricity Meter.

synergies.why: Held unspent, the 3 free restocks give +6 Symbols Multiplier.
Each restock adds +2 to Bell Pepper's Luck for the Deadline.
Three restocks recharge three Red Button charges.
Abyssu banks a second activation: discard Abyssu later for 3 more free restocks.

summary: Every 7th spin, all Patterns trigger one extra time.
tip: A small, steady boost (about 1 spin in 7 doubled). Collect all three Discs to fuse them into Platinum Record (DLC).

synergies.why: Surgery: Disc A + B + C fuse into Platinum Record, an effect every 2 spins (DLC).
Surgery: Disc A + B + C fuse into Platinum Record (DLC).
The doubled spin is more likely to reach 5+ Patterns.

assumptions: Assumed to count spins continuously across Rounds (not restarting each Round); which spin of the Round it lands on is unverified.

summary: Every 7th spin gets Luck +7.
tip: A 1-ticket guaranteed Luck +7 spin every 7 spins, about what Rotated Hamsa gives on 7-spin Rounds. Also part of the Platinum Record fusion (DLC).

synergies.why: Surgery: Disc A + B + C fuse into Platinum Record (DLC).
Surgery: Disc A + B + C fuse into Platinum Record (DLC).
Its Luck comes from the charm, so it survives Depression and gives a no-Luck build a reliable scoring spin.

assumptions: Assumed to count spins continuously across Rounds (not restarting each Round).

summary: Every 7th spin is forced to show both the ZIG and ZAG patterns.
tip: ZIG + ZAG (pattern value 4 each) every 7 spins for 1 ticket: strong early and still fine later. Grows with large-pattern value boosts.

synergies.why: Surgery: Disc A + B + C fuse into Platinum Record (DLC).
Surgery: Disc A + B + C fuse into Platinum Record (DLC).
+base value on ZIG and ZAG (and every other 4+ pattern).
Doubles all 4+ symbol patterns, including ZIG and ZAG.
The forced ZIG and ZAG are 4+ symbol patterns, so every 7th spin permanently raises Diamonds and Treasures.

assumptions: ZIG and ZAG share two middle cells, so both come out in the same symbol (8 cells).
Assumed to count spins continuously across Rounds (not restarting each Round).

summary: Takes no space: permanently gives +1 charm slot. Once used, it never shows up in the store again.
tip: Buy it whenever you see it. A permanent slot outlasts almost any other 2-ticket purchase.

effects.text: Once used, it never shows up in the store again this run.

synergies.why: Bank it with Abyssu to use it a second time for another +1 slot.
Offsets Megaphone's -1 charm space.
One more charm on the table adds resell value to Dark Lotus.

summary: Every store restock recharges 1 charge on a random equipped Red Button charm.
tip: Turns spare coins into charges. Best with 1-2 strong button charms so the random charge isn't spread thin.

synergies.why: Restock charges refill its 4-charge cost, so it can be switched on in more Rounds.
Every few restocks become another permanent +1 Symbols Multiplier.
Restocks feed its 12-charge extra Round.
Every press the restock charges pay for triggers twice.
3 free restocks = 3 charges.
That memory card stops Round-end recharging, so restock charges become your main fuel.

antiSynergies.why: The Cart rewards hoarding free restocks instead of spending them.

summary: After 2 spins in a row with no reward, all equipped Red Button charms gain 1 charge.
tip: Cheap fuel for button builds, strongest early when missed spins are common. Useless without Red Button charms.

synergies.why: Extra charges turn into permanent Symbols Multiplier.
Refills its 4 charges faster for more growth Rounds.
Extra charges flip the Cross more often, growing its Patterns Multiplier.
Helps refill the 12 charges it needs.
Without spontaneous Luck, 2-miss streaks happen more often.
Another charge source; with Super Capacitor and Dynamo they fuse into Exotic Matter (DLC).

assumptions: Assumed to fire once per pair of missed spins (the miss count restarts after it fires).

summary: 10% chance each spin to grant 1 extra spin with Luck +4.
tip: Small but permanent. Horseshoe doubles it to 20%; an extra spin gained on a Round's last spin gives Rotated Hamsa another Luck +7 spin.

synergies.why: Doubles its chance to 20%.
Red Button forces its extra lucky spin.
An extra spin gained on the last spin becomes a new last spin, so Rotated Hamsa gives Luck +7 again.
More spins mean more 3+ Pattern payouts.
Surgery (DLC): Fake Coin + Shopping Cart fuse into RWD Cart.

assumptions: In the game the extra spin and its Luck +4 come from one 10% roll; the engine cannot put Luck on the extra spin, so the Luck is encoded as its own 10% roll on a normal spin (similar average value).
Calibration: tier raised to B; at 1 ticket its extra spins and Luck rank in the top quarter of picks across typical builds.
Engine: Luck +4 applies to the extra spin itself (spins.luck).

summary: Red Button (1 charge): after the next spin you get an extra spin with Luck +7. It may break after its 3rd use.
tip: Press it every Round; it regains its charge each Round. Pressed before the last spin, the extra spin also gets Rotated Hamsa's Luck +7. Cheap to rebuy when it breaks.

effects.text: After its 3rd use it has a 15% chance per Round to be discarded when it activates (roughly 9 uses on average).

synergies.why: Each press gives two extra Luck +7 spins.
Pressed before the last spin, its extra spin becomes a new last spin and also gets Rotated Hamsa's Luck +7.
With another fully charged button charm equipped, it can refill this single charge between spins.
A pair of missed spins recharges it for another lucky spin.
When it finally breaks, the discard feeds Dung Beetle.

assumptions: Discard rule read as: once used 3 times, each activation has a 15% chance (at most once per Round) to discard it.
The engine gives the Luck +7 to the next spin rather than to the extra spin; total value is about the same.
Engine: Luck +7 applies to the extra spin itself (spins.luck).

summary: +2 spins every Round.
tip: About 28% more spins on the 7-spin option and 67% more on the 3-spin option. Good in nearly every build.

synergies.why: Surgery (DLC): Cat Food + Toy Train fuse into Cat Toy (+2 spins with Luck +8 after 3 straight misses).
More spins mean more 3+ Pattern payouts.
More spins per Round to grow its multiplier.
With 1-spin Rounds, +2 spins triples your spins.

summary: Removes the slot machine's own spontaneous Luck; Luck from charms still works.
tip: A drawback in normal builds. Take it only for no-reward builds (Locomotives, Bullet Train) that want more empty spins.

effects.text: The slot machine's spontaneous Luck (lucky-spark spins and pity Luck after missed spins) is set to 0. Luck granted by charms still applies.

synergies.why: Empty Rounds double both multipliers; without free Luck, zero-coin Rounds come far more often.
Fewer lucky spins mean more 3-miss streaks.
Fewer lucky spins mean more 3-miss streaks.
More empty spins to roll its 25% on.
More 2-miss streaks, so more recharges.
Cat Toy (DLC) gives +2 spins with Luck +8 after 3 straight misses; without spontaneous Luck those streaks come more often.

assumptions: Assumed to also remove the pity Luck the machine gives after long miss streaks.

summary: After 2 spins with no reward, the next spin gets Luck +5 (+2 more for each extra miss in a row).
tip: Softens dry streaks early. Avoid it with Steam or Diesel Locomotive: its Luck breaks their 3-miss streaks.

effects.text: If the boosted spin also misses, the next one gets 2 more Luck (5, 7, 9...) until a spin pays.

synergies.why: Surgery (DLC): Toy Train + Cat Food fuse into Cat Toy.

antiSynergies.why: Its Luck after 2 misses often breaks the 3-miss streak the Locomotive needs.
Its Luck after 2 misses often breaks the 3-miss streak the Locomotive needs.

assumptions: Escalation read as +5, +7, +9... Luck while the miss streak continues; it resets after a rewarded spin.

summary: After 3 spins in a row with no reward, every symbol permanently gains its base value.
tip: Free scaling from bad spins, strongest early. Pairs with Diesel Locomotive. Don't run Toy Train with it: its Luck breaks the streaks.

synergies.why: Same trigger, and symbol and pattern growth multiply. The two fuse into Bullet Train (DLC).
Removes the lucky and pity spins that break miss streaks.
An empty spin is also a miss toward the 3-miss streak, so the same bad spins feed both symbol-value boosts.

antiSynergies.why: Its Luck after 2 misses often breaks the 3-miss streak.

assumptions: Unclear whether a 4th straight miss triggers it again or the count restarts after it fires.

summary: After 3 spins in a row with no reward, every Pattern permanently gains its base value.
tip: Grows all pattern values from bad spins and multiplies with Steam Locomotive. Don't run Toy Train with it: its Luck breaks the streaks.

synergies.why: Same trigger, and symbol and pattern growth multiply. The two fuse into Bullet Train (DLC).
Removes the lucky and pity spins that break miss streaks.
Each trigger adds +7 to Above and Below (their base value); Nose forces one of them every few spins.

antiSynergies.why: Its Luck after 2 misses often breaks the 3-miss streak.

assumptions: Unclear whether a 4th straight miss triggers it again or the count restarts after it fires.
